findings.title: Superseded Runs Not Cancelled (Missing Concurrency or `cancel-in-progress: false`)
findings.evidence: 9 run(s) across 5 branch(es) were superseded (a newer run started before they finished) in the sampled window; ~2–13 runner-min/mo of superseded compute (mean over 20 timed run(s); ×0.06 to the 30d volume (6 runs); 100-run recent slice (not a full 30d census)). Superseded attribution is INFERENCE — the API marks no run 'cancelled-by-concurrency'.
findings.measured_signal: overlap-confirmed superseded runs x mean job-minutes (9 confirmed; naive 79; 20 timed run(s); scale 0.06)
findings.size_note: runner-minute (bill) only — superseded runs don't gate the merge (the latest run does); range is lower(overlap-confirmed)–upper(naive runs-1).

measured_evidence.summary: 9 run(s) across 5 branch(es) were superseded (a newer run started before they finished) in the sampled window; ~2–13 runner-min/mo of superseded compute (mean over 20 timed run(s); ×0.06 to the 30d volume (6 runs); 100-run recent slice (not a full 30d census)). Superseded attribution is INFERENCE — the API marks no run 'cancelled-by-concurrency'.
measured_evidence.note: Superseded = a run a NEWER run started before it finished — measured by timestamp overlap, so sequential (non-racing) commits are NOT charged. Cancellation cause is unknowable from the API, so the attribution is INFERENCE. Basis: the count is from the all-status slice (100 runs); the per-run PRICE is the mean of 20 PR-success timed runs (superseded runs' own jobs aren't fetched) — different populations. GUARDRAIL: verify this is NOT a deploy/release/publish workflow (a mid-flight run may be uploading artifacts / pushing a tag) before enabling cancellation — and take the predicate from the catalog recipe, which scopes cancellation with an expression; never a bare `cancel-in-progress: true`, which also kills in-flight runs on the default branch and on release tags. ROUTING: this workflow triggers on `pull_request` — with a `pull_request` trigger use the catalog's DEFAULT (PR-scoped) predicate; without one, the PR-scoped predicate is never true and saves nothing, so use the catalog's WIDENED predicate.

tier2_neutrality.ref: superseded runs: same head_branch, a newer run started before this one finished (timestamp overlap); cancellation cause is inference

findings.title: Matrix Leg Imbalance
findings.evidence: leg `Analyze (java, none, true)` median 103s vs `Analyze (actions, none)` 36s — 2.9× imbalance over 18 sampled runs (heterogeneous legs — split the slow leg, don't rebalance)
findings.measured_signal: leg `Analyze (java, none, true)` median 103s vs `Analyze (actions, none)` 36s — 2.9× imbalance over 18 sampled runs (heterogeneous legs — split the slow leg, don't rebalance)
findings.size_note: split the slow leg `Analyze (java, none, true)`; saving (~52s) is bounded by the next-slowest leg (36s); population-weighted measured floor — the merge gate is bimodal, so the critical path differs by PR; this check is the pole on ~0/20 PR populations (sampled PRs that ran a gated check), giving an expected Δ 0s of the 52s raw saving

measured_evidence.summary: Across 18 sampled `Analyze` runs, the slowest leg (`Analyze (java, none, true)`, median 103s) is 2.9× the fastest (`Analyze (actions, none)`, 36s) and gates the matrix. These legs do DIFFERENT work, so they cannot be rebalanced — the slow leg is the long pole.
measured_evidence.note: Each link opens that leg's worst observed run. Fix: SPLIT the slowest leg `Analyze (java, none, true)` itself (sub-shard its suite, or split its backends into parallel jobs) — not rebalance across legs. That floors at the next-slowest leg `Analyze (actions, none)` (36s), which becomes the new pole, so the realistic first-step saving is ~52s; split that leg next to go lower.

wall_clock_derivation.reason: population-weighted measured floor — the merge gate is bimodal, so the critical path differs by PR; this check is the pole on ~0/20 PR populations (sampled PRs that ran a gated check), giving an expected Δ 0s of the 52s raw saving
